rows.scenario: R06–R12 and R19–R20 native crash and lifecycle faults
rows.environment: Node on Debian Linux, Chrome callbacks mocked
rows.expectedOutcome: Healthy rows survive; one current owner; stale routes cannot save.
rows.baselineOutcome: Lost create callback after removeAll erased the only native row.
rows.actualOutcome: Unaffected row remained; 20 cold activations shared stable IDs, one listener, and no menu journal rewrites.
rows.remainingRisk: Original Windows profile and Chrome native sibling order are open.

rows.scenario: R01–R05 and R15–R17 empty, login, reconnect, offline and visibility
rows.testMethod: Canonical API native lifecycle fixture and existing visibility tests
rows.environment: Node on Debian Linux, Chrome callbacks mocked
rows.expectedOutcome: Visible providers remain independent of OAuth and setup.
rows.baselineOutcome: Ordinary evaluation did not reconcile; blocked setup with empty configuration could skip reconciliation.
rows.actualOutcome: Four provider actions from validated empty state. Login schedules native reconcile when OAuth connects and initialization remains blocked.
rows.remainingRisk: Actual post-login Chrome and R2 behavior are open.

rows.scenario: R13–R14 and R17 exact target authority
rows.testMethod: Simple, Narrow, Depth, Default and Quick tests and local workerd R2
rows.expectedOutcome: Only the exact current and authorized destination receives a save.
rows.actualOutcome: Existing binding, readback and idempotency tests exercise exact targets; wrong accounts and stale IDs fail closed.
rows.remainingRisk: Live R2 readback and real native ordering are open.

rows.testMethod: Measured Node fixture and saturated production transport
rows.expectedOutcome: Independent operation IDs, no wrong target writes and bounded admitted remote work.
rows.baselineOutcome: Not measured against the diagnostic tag.
rows.actualOutcome: Unique exact-target fixture dispatch and 32 transport slots; overflow returned RESOURCE_BUSY.
rows.remainingRisk: Actual browser process sampling and provider performance are open.

rows.scenario: B02–B04 screenshot bursts and logged-out exception
rows.testMethod: Screenshot runner and Chrome quota fixtures
rows.expectedOutcome: At most 2 capture slots, 6 upload tasks and zero logged-out jobs.
rows.baselineOutcome: Runner wrote pending before checking authority and lacked a total capture bound.
rows.actualOutcome: 10/50/100 burst fixtures admitted 2 per run. No logged-out captures, uploads, retry entries or History rows. An accepted session-change job retained its blocked receipt.
rows.remainingRisk: Actual browser capture quota behavior and process memory remain open.

rows.environment: Chromium 156 on Linux, actual IndexedDB and production Shelf
rows.expectedOutcome: Open History tracks both job types and batches IDs; reopening displays durable items.
rows.baselineOutcome: A burst of more than 64 distinct IDs could reload the entire archive.
rows.actualOutcome: 132 IDs over 2301 previous rows used 64/64/4 lookups. Both operation types updated and reopened, with keyboard focus retained.
rows.remainingRisk: Real native and live provider messaging remain open.

rows.scenario: B08 Mixed activity across simulated worker wake
rows.testMethod: Held screenshot upload and separately reconstructed production registrar
rows.environment: Node on Debian Linux, Chrome callbacks mocked
rows.expectedOutcome: Screenshot tasks do not starve native menu registration or dispatch.
rows.actualOutcome: Cold registrar re-ACKed while upload was held; deterministic dispatch and listener/byte cleanup passed.
rows.remainingRisk: Actual MV3 teardown with in-flight work remains open.

rows.scenario: R18, R21–R22 and B09 installed browser and live provider
rows.testMethod: Headed Chromium unpacked extension load and independent Windows/R2 evidence requirements
rows.expectedOutcome: Visually rendered native Chrome menu, verified object readback, original-profile regression and Windows per-process memory.
rows.baselineOutcome: Protected baseline symptom reproduced only in a fault fixture.
rows.actualOutcome: Administrator disabled unpacked extensions. Windows Chrome and live R2 access unavailable.
rows.remainingRisk: No Chrome menu registration ACK, genuine visible menu, live Worker request or independently verified R2 write for this release.
